title: SharePoint Site Storage Utilization
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'SharePoint Site Storage Utilization' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_sharepoint_site_storage_utilization` (UC-11.3.22), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — SharePoint Site Storage Utilization", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=sharepoint` sourcetype='sharepoint:site_usage' that satisfy the UC-11.3.22 SPL filters for 'SharePoint Site Storage Utilization'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `sharepoint` / `sharepoint:site_usage` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-11.3.22.

dataSources: SharePoint REST API (/_api/site/usage), Get-SPOSite (SharePoint Online) Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Custom (SharePoint REST API, PowerShell) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=sharepoint sourcetype="sharepoint:site_usage"
| eval used_mb=coalesce(StorageUsageCurrent/1024, StorageUsageCurrentMB, 0), quota_mb=coalesce(StorageQuota/1024, StorageQuotaMB, 0)
| eval used_pct=if(quota_mb>0, round(used_mb/quota_mb*100, 1), 0)
| where used_pct >= 70
| bin _time span=1d
| stats latest(used_mb) as used_mb, latest(quota_mb) as quota_mb, latest(used_pct) as used_pct by _time, SiteUrl, SiteName
| where used_pct >= 70
| sort -used_pct
| table SiteUrl, SiteName, used_mb, quota_mb, used_pct

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance** — Planned change generates expected deviations for 'SharePoint Site Storage Utilization'. Cross-check change records.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Custom (SharePoint REST API, PowerShell).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: SharePoint REST API (/_api/site/usage), Get-SPOSite (SharePoint Online).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
For SharePoint Online, use `Get-SPOSite -IncludePersonalSite $false | Select-Object Url, StorageUsageCurrent, StorageQuota` via a scheduled PowerShell script; for on-prem, call `/_api/site/usage` with app-only or user credentials. Forward JSON to Splunk via HEC. Run daily or every 6 hours. Alert when used_pct >= 80 (warning) or >= 95 (critical). Maintain a lookup of site owners for notification. Report on growth rate and projected quota exhaustion.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=sharepoint sourcetype="sharepoint:site_usage"
| eval used_mb=coalesce(StorageUsageCurrent/1024, StorageUsageCurrentMB, 0), quota_mb=coalesce(StorageQuota/1024, StorageQuotaMB, 0)
| eval used_pct=if(quota_mb>0, round(used_mb/quota_mb*100, 1), 0)
| where used_pct >= 70
| bin _time span=1d
| stats latest(used_mb) as used_mb, latest(quota_mb) as quota_mb, latest(used_pct) as used_pct by _time, SiteUrl, SiteName
| where used_pct >= 70
| sort -used_pct
| table SiteUrl, SiteName, used_mb, quota_mb, used_pct
```

Understanding this SPL

**SharePoint Site Storage Utilization** — Site collections approaching quota block uploads and disrupt teams. Proactive monitoring enables quota increases or content archival before users hit limits.

Documented **Data sources**: SharePoint REST API (/_api/site/usage), Get-SPOSite (SharePoint Online). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Custom (SharePoint REST API, PowerShell). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: sharepoint; **sourcetype**: sharepoint:site_usage. If that sourcetype is not mentioned in Data sources, double-check parsing or update the documentation to match the feed you actually ingest.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=sharepoint, sourcetype="sharepoint:site_usage". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **used_mb** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **used_pct** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where used_pct >= 70` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Discretizes time or numeric ranges with `bin`/`bucket`.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by _time, SiteUrl, SiteName** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• Filters the current rows with `where used_pct >= 70` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.
• Pipeline stage (see **SharePoint Site Storage Utilization**): table SiteUrl, SiteName, used_mb, quota_mb, used_pct


Step 3 — Validate
Compare with SharePoint admin, storage metrics, and search service (if applicable) in the same farm or Microsoft 365 tenant for the time window.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Table (sites near quota), Bar chart (usage by site), Gauge (overall tenant usage %), Line chart (storage growth trend).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Custom (SharePoint REST API, PowerShell) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=sharepoint:site_usage into sharepoint. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`SiteName, SiteUrl, _time, quota_mb`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
